# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 11
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 11

---

*[Thomas in prison. A miraculous release. More miracles and conversions. The king confronts Thomas.]*

1. And when Thomas was in prison, Mygdonia came to him by night and said: "I beg you, servant of God, come out of prison, for we have need of you."

2. And Thomas said: "Has the door been opened, or how shall I come out?"

3. And she said: "The doors have been opened and your fetters are loosed."

4. And Thomas went out and said: "Blessed be the Lord, for his mercy upon me is great."

5. And many came to him in the night and he taught them and baptized them.

6. And when morning came, the king heard that Thomas had gone out of prison and the doors were not broken. And the king was greatly astonished.

7. And he sent for Thomas and said to him: "Who opened the prison for you?"

8. And Thomas said: "Ask those who have the keys."

9. And the king said to the guards: "Did you open the prison for him?"

10. And they said: "My lord, the doors were not opened, nor did we open them. We found them secured and sealed as we had left them, but Thomas is gone."

11. And the king was astonished and troubled and did not know what to think of this man.

12. And Thomas went again and taught and baptized many in those days.

13. And a woman came to Thomas who was the wife of a certain man who was one of the nobles of the city. And she said: "I have a son who is greatly troubled by a demon, and I beg you in the name of your Lord to heal him."

14. And Thomas had compassion on her and went with her and prayed over her son. And the demon departed and the young man was healed.

15. And the king heard these things and was troubled, for he did not know what to do with Thomas, for many were following him.

16. And Charisius came again to the king and said: "Command this man to be removed from here, for he is seducing all your people."

17. And the king said to Thomas: "You must leave our borders."

18. And Thomas said: "I will go wherever my Lord commands me."

19. And the king said: "We shall see. Until then remain in this city."

20. And Thomas remained and went about teaching and baptizing.

---
*EMET note: The miraculous prison release (vv.3–4) is a standard element of the apostolic-acts genre (cf. Acts 5:19, 12:7–10). The locked-but-empty prison motif validates the apostle's divine commission.*
